data.body: Final debug report. Problem: MCP transition/claim omitted supported library write controls. Proven cause: FastMCP derives input models from the stale handwritten signatures and drops undeclared extras; the handwritten delegate calls independently omitted the same values. Proof: live-schema/capture, declared-field control, two-commit ref, and caused_by differential probes all isolated the adapter boundary. Test: the final held-out real-FastMCP oracle was RED on all five slices before repair, GREEN after repair, returned to RED when signatures were removed, and returned to RED separately when forwarding was removed. It asserts public schema and persisted outcomes, so behavior-preserving refactors do not break it. Fix: transition_ticket now exposes and forwards bool force, reason, caused_by, and optional ref; claim_ticket exposes and forwards reason-bearing optional force; tool prose records absent certification as the audit signal; force_close remains absent. Scope/safety: all callers converge on the existing library/core; no behavioral dependency on the unreachable fields, no new dependency, no weakened test, and _mcp_writes.py remains 570 lines. Focused MCP, surface, close-ref, and plan-gate matrix collected 143 tests and passed; make lint and make typecheck pass. Parity census: CLI and library already enforce the rule; MCP is fixed at the shared adapter; automated callers use the library/core and need no change; dual-direction is N/A. Sibling sweep found relation-specific unlink missing only on MCP; filed and linked airy-starchy-muntjac. Import-only source provenance, internal placeholder identity tags, generic edit fields, and the separately governed CLI-only secret override were not confirmed siblings. Original reason-required close, caused_by, ref pin/sign, and both force scenarios now succeed through the real registered MCP tools; absent force and absent required reason remain rejected.
